newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks seen rangebound, thinly traded.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks seen rangebound, thinly traded.

text.p: Argentine stocks were seen little changed at the opening Monday in muted trade ahead of the release of a battery of U.S. economic indicators, dealers said.

"My clients are staying on the sidelines today," one trader said. "Nobody wants to risk losing last week's gains because Wall Street may take a hit if the indicators show inflationary pressures, especially those related to wages due out Tuesday and Friday."
The blue-chip MerVal index rose 0.8 percent to 715.48 Friday, stretching the week's gains to 1.7 percent.
But floor volume shrank to a puny 12.7 million pesos Friday from a healthy daily tally of 29 pesos managed twice earlier in the week.

Traders said the market had quickly run out of steam after a recent two-day rally sparked by Standard and Poor's corporate credit rating upgrades, which raised the bonds of several firms to investment-grade.
"Today investors will be watching the U.S. long bond yield and little else," another trader said. "The S&P news was unable to break our huge New York dependency."
